title: Examining AI Use in Educational Contexts: A Scoping Meta-Review and Bibliometric Analysis
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly expanding literature on artificial intelligence in education (AIED) by synthesizing existing systematic reviews rather than primary studies. The authors note that while many systematic reviews have examined AI applications across educational settings, fewer studies had synthesized those reviews to provide a panoramic view of the field. To fill that gap, they conducted a scoping meta-review and bibliometric analysis of systematic reviews on AI use in education, following PRISMA guidelines.

The paper does not study a direct classroom intervention; instead, it reviews 126 systematic reviews published between 2014 and mid-August 2023, drawing from Scopus and Web of Science. The included reviews span PreK-12 and higher education contexts and cover topics such as machine learning, intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, data mining, adaptive and personalized learning, AI-based assessment, instructional pedagogies, teacher roles, curriculum design, teacher professional development, student performance prediction, administrative efficiency, and institutional services. The analysis combines keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship, geographic mapping, and thematic synthesis.

The authors conclude that machine learning is the most frequently studied AI approach in educational review literature, with much of the research concentrated in Asia and Europe and a strong emphasis on higher education. They identify three major thematic areas: AI’s impact on learning, teaching, and administration. The paper argues that AI is often discussed in terms of potential benefits, especially for adaptive learning, personalization, assessment, and decision support, but that the literature is uneven, with limited attention to learning context details, student demographics, and teacher preparation. It calls for more granular, context-sensitive, and theoretically grounded future research, especially around teacher development, curriculum design, and underexplored educational settings.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: Intelligent tutoring systems are AI-driven instructional systems that provide adaptive guidance, feedback, and support during learning.
identified_tools.use_case: This scoping meta-review synthesized prior systematic reviews on AI in education, including reviews discussing intelligent tutoring systems as one AI approach among many.

findings.finding_summary: The paper reports that intelligent tutoring systems were one of the most widely studied AI approaches in the reviewed literature, appearing in the keyword/network analysis and in the synthesis of prior reviews. It also notes that ITSs were discussed as supporting learning, teaching, and assessment, but the paper does not report a pooled effect size for ITS specifically.
findings.measure: Frequency of ITS mention across included systematic reviews; thematic synthesis of prior review findings
findings.sample_size: 126 reviews in the meta-review; underlying ITS-study sample sizes not reported

identified_tools.name: Machine Learning
identified_tools.description: Machine learning is a family of data-driven computational methods used to identify patterns, make predictions, and support adaptive decision-making.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper identified machine learning as the most frequently studied AI type across the included systematic reviews and discussed its roles in educational analytics, prediction, and instructional support.

findings.finding_summary: Machine learning was the most frequently studied AI type in the included reviews, with 43 appearances in the paper's AI-application count. The authors also describe machine learning as underpinning adaptive systems, learning analytics, prediction, and other education applications, but no pooled causal estimate is reported.
findings.measure: Frequency of machine learning across included systematic reviews; thematic synthesis of prior review findings
findings.sample_size: 126 reviews in the meta-review; underlying study samples not reported

identified_tools.name: Learning Analytics
identified_tools.description: Learning analytics systems analyze learner data to support prediction, monitoring, and decision-making in education.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper synthesized prior reviews that examined learning analytics in educational contexts, especially for teaching, performance monitoring, and administrative decision support.

findings.finding_summary: Learning analytics appeared among the most prominent keywords and was discussed as a major AI application in education, especially for predicting performance, supporting instructional decisions, and informing administration. The paper does not provide pooled effect sizes for learning analytics outcomes.
findings.measure: Keyword co-occurrence and thematic synthesis of prior reviews
findings.sample_size: 126 reviews in the meta-review; underlying study samples not reported

quality_tier_rationale: This is a scoping meta-review and bibliometric analysis of systematic reviews, not a primary intervention study or meta-analysis of effect sizes. The evidence is useful for mapping the field, but it does not establish causal effects for any one tool.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests broad, positive educational relevance for AI approaches such as machine learning, ITS, and learning analytics, but it reports no effect sizes for these tools. Impact is therefore directional and field-mapping in nature rather than quantitatively demonstrated.
